\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{از} \fa{طرف} \fa{دیگر} (az taraf-e digar)}{از طرف دیگر (az taraf-e digar)}]{\fa{از} \fa{طرف} \fa{دیگر} (az taraf-e digar) — on the other hand}

\label{lesson:FA-C367-az-taraf-e-digar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for an objection, then the Persian for to give an example.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{از} \fa{طرف} \fa{دیگر}}
\textbf{\fa{از} \fa{طرف} \fa{دیگر}} (\emph{az taraf-e digar}) — \textquotedblleft{}on the other hand\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{این} \fa{خانه} \fa{بزرگ} \fa{است}. \fa{از} \fa{طرف} \fa{دیگر،} \fa{خیلی} \fa{گران} \fa{است}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{in khâne bozorg ast. az taraf-e digar, kheyli gerân ast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
This house is big. On the other hand, it is very expensive.
\end{quote}

Often paired with \emph{az yek taraf} \textquotedblleft{}on the one hand\textquotedblright{}. A whole clause follows it.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{از} \fa{طرف} \fa{دیگر}} is literally \textquotedblleft{}from the other side\textquotedblright{}: \emph{az} \textquotedblleft{}from\textquotedblright{} and \emph{digar} \textquotedblleft{}other\textquotedblright{} are inherited Persian (EtymDB traces \emph{digar} to PIE \emph{dwóh\textsubscript{1}} \textquotedblleft{}two\textquotedblright{}), and \emph{taraf} was borrowed from Arabic \emph{ṭaraf} \textquotedblleft{}side\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{az taraf-e digar}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{az taraf-e digar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{az taraf-e digar}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for an objection, then the Persian for to give an example, then say \emph{az taraf-e digar} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{به} \fa{عبارت} \fa{دیگر} (be 'ebârat-e digar)}{به عبارت دیگر (be 'ebârat-e digar)}]{\fa{به} \fa{عبارت} \fa{دیگر} (be 'ebârat-e digar) — in other words}

\label{lesson:FA-C367-be-ebarat-e-digar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to give an example, then the Persian for on the other hand.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{به} \fa{عبارت} \fa{دیگر}}
\textbf{\fa{به} \fa{عبارت} \fa{دیگر}} (\emph{be 'ebârat-e digar}) — \textquotedblleft{}in other words\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{او} \fa{کار} \fa{را} \fa{تمام} \fa{نکرد}. \fa{به} \fa{عبارت} \fa{دیگر،} \fa{فردا} \fa{باید} \fa{دوباره} \fa{بیاید}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{u kâr râ tamâm nakard. be 'ebârat-e digar, fardâ bâyad dobâre biyâyad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He did not finish the job. In other words, he has to come again tomorrow.
\end{quote}

\emph{Be} \textquotedblleft{}with\textquotedblright{} + \emph{'ebârat} \textquotedblleft{}an expression\textquotedblright{} + \emph{digar} \textquotedblleft{}other\textquotedblright{}. It restates the same idea in plainer words.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{به} \fa{عبارت} \fa{دیگر}} joins \emph{'ebârat}, from Arabic \emph{'ibāra} \textquotedblleft{}an expression\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), to the inherited Persian words \emph{be} and \emph{digar} \textquotedblleft{}other\textquotedblright{}: in another expression.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{be 'ebârat-e digar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{be 'ebârat-e digar}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to give an example, then the Persian for on the other hand, then say \emph{be 'ebârat-e digar} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{اما} (ammâ)}{اما (ammâ)}]{\fa{اما} (ammâ) — but, however}

\label{lesson:FA-C367-amma}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for on the other hand, then the Persian for in other words.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{اما}}
\textbf{\fa{اما}} (\emph{ammâ}) — \textquotedblleft{}but, however\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{هوا} \fa{سرد} \fa{بود،} \fa{اما} \fa{ما} \fa{بیرون} \fa{رفتیم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{havâ sard bud, ammâ mâ birun raftim.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
It was cold, but we went out.
\end{quote}

A little more formal than \emph{vali}; both join two clauses, and \emph{ammâ} can also open a sentence.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{اما}} comes from Arabic \emph{ammā} \textquotedblleft{}as for, as regards\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB); Persian uses it to mean \textquotedblleft{}but\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ammâ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ammâ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{ammâ}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for on the other hand, then the Persian for in other words, then say \emph{ammâ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{با} \fa{این} \fa{وجود} (bâ in vojud)}{با این وجود (bâ in vojud)}]{\fa{با} \fa{این} \fa{وجود} (bâ in vojud) — nevertheless, even so}

\label{lesson:FA-C367-ba-in-vojud}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for in other words, then the Persian for but.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{با} \fa{این} \fa{وجود}}
\textbf{\fa{با} \fa{این} \fa{وجود}} (\emph{bâ in vojud}) — \textquotedblleft{}nevertheless, even so\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{باران} \fa{میآمد}. \fa{با} \fa{این} \fa{وجود،} \fa{مسابقه} \fa{ادامه} \fa{پیدا} \fa{کرد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{bârân miâmad. bâ in vojud, mosâbeqe edâme peydâ kard.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
It was raining. Nevertheless, the match went on.
\end{quote}

Like \emph{bâ in hâl}; a whole clause follows it. Compare \emph{bâ vojud-e} + a noun, \textquotedblleft{}despite\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{با} \fa{این} \fa{وجود}} is literally \textquotedblleft{}with this existing\textquotedblright{}: \emph{bâ} \textquotedblleft{}with\textquotedblright{} and \emph{in} \textquotedblleft{}this\textquotedblright{} are inherited Persian, and \emph{vojud} comes from Arabic \emph{wujūd} \textquotedblleft{}existence\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for in other words, then the Persian for but, then say \emph{bâ in vojud} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{هرچند} (harchand)}{هرچند (harchand)}]{\fa{هرچند} (harchand) — although, even though}

\label{lesson:FA-C367-harchand}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for but, then the Persian for nevertheless.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{هرچند}}
\textbf{\fa{هرچند}} (\emph{harchand}) — \textquotedblleft{}although, even though\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{هرچند} \fa{خسته} \fa{بودم،} \fa{تا} \fa{آخر} \fa{فیلم} \fa{را} \fa{دیدم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{harchand khaste budam, tâ âkhar film râ didam.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Although I was tired, I watched the film to the end.
\end{quote}

Takes an indicative clause, like \emph{agarche}; the main clause follows without a linking word.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{هرچند}} is a native Persian compound built from \emph{har} \textquotedblleft{}every\textquotedblright{} and \emph{chand} \textquotedblleft{}how many, however much\textquotedblright{}: however much that is so, the main clause still holds.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{harchand}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{harchand}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{harchand}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for but, then the Persian for nevertheless, then say \emph{harchand} again
\end{itemize}

\section[(dialogue)]{Reasons and opinions — a review}

\label{lesson:FA-R367-review-360-367}



\begin{quote}
Say the Persian for an opinion and a point of view.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item an opinion, a point of view, an attitude, to believe, a theory
  \item to agree, to oppose, opposed, to believe in, to doubt
  \item an argument, to argue, logic, logical, to convince
  \item a claim, to claim, to prove, to be proven, evidence
  \item a fact, the truth, in fact, a rumour, to deny
  \item to judge, criticism, to criticise, to exaggerate, to justify
  \item a discussion, to discuss, a negotiation, an objection, to give an example
  \item on the other hand, in other words, but, nevertheless, although
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
An opinion? (\textbf{\fa{عقیده}}.) A point of view? (\textbf{\fa{دیدگاه}}.) An attitude? (\textbf{\fa{نگرش}}.) To believe? (\textbf{\fa{معتقد} \fa{بودن}}.) A theory? (\textbf{\fa{نظریه}}.) To agree? (\textbf{\fa{موافقت} \fa{کردن}}.) To oppose? (\textbf{\fa{مخالفت} \fa{کردن}}.) Opposed? (\textbf{\fa{مخالف}}.) To believe in? (\textbf{\fa{باور} \fa{داشتن}}.) To doubt? (\textbf{\fa{شک} \fa{داشتن}}.) An argument? (\textbf{\fa{استدلال}}.) To argue? (\textbf{\fa{استدلال} \fa{کردن}}.) Logic? (\textbf{\fa{منطق}}.) Logical? (\textbf{\fa{منطقی}}.) To convince? (\textbf{\fa{قانع} \fa{کردن}}.) A claim? (\textbf{\fa{ادعا}}.) To claim? (\textbf{\fa{ادعا} \fa{کردن}}.) To prove? (\textbf{\fa{اثبات} \fa{کردن}}.) To be proven? (\textbf{\fa{ثابت} \fa{شدن}}.) Evidence? (\textbf{\fa{شواهد}}.) A fact? (\textbf{\fa{واقعیت}}.) The truth? (\textbf{\fa{حقیقت}}.) In fact? (\textbf{\fa{در} \fa{واقع}}.) A rumour? (\textbf{\fa{شایعه}}.) To deny? (\textbf{\fa{انکار} \fa{کردن}}.) To judge? (\textbf{\fa{قضاوت} \fa{کردن}}.) Criticism? (\textbf{\fa{انتقاد}}.) To criticise? (\textbf{\fa{انتقاد} \fa{کردن}}.) To exaggerate? (\textbf{\fa{اغراق} \fa{کردن}}.) To justify? (\textbf{\fa{توجیه} \fa{کردن}}.) A discussion? (\textbf{\fa{بحث}}.) To discuss? (\textbf{\fa{بحث} \fa{کردن}}.) A negotiation? (\textbf{\fa{مذاکره}}.) An objection? (\textbf{\fa{اعتراض}}.) To give an example? (\textbf{\fa{مثال} \fa{زدن}}.) On the other hand? (\textbf{\fa{از} \fa{طرف} \fa{دیگر}}.) In other words? (\textbf{\fa{به} \fa{عبارت} \fa{دیگر}}.) But? (\textbf{\fa{اما}}.) Nevertheless? (\textbf{\fa{با} \fa{این} \fa{وجود}}.) Although? (\textbf{\fa{هرچند}}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
